bullets.text: ML is a subfield of AI focused on systems learning from data without explicit programming.
Systems identify patterns and make decisions with minimal human intervention.
Used in image recognition, NLP, predictive analytics, and autonomous vehicles.
Growth driven by large datasets, improved computational power, and advanced algorithms.
Broadly classified into Supervised, Unsupervised, and Reinforcement Learning.
Supervised Learning: Trains on labeled data to predict outputs (Regression, Classification).
Unsupervised Learning: Finds hidden patterns in unlabeled data (Clustering, Dimensionality Reduction).
Reinforcement Learning: Agent learns by interacting with environment to maximize rewards.
Model Training: Feeding data to learn patterns and minimize prediction errors.
Features and Labels: Input variables (features) and target outputs (labels) in supervised learning.
Training and Testing Sets: Data split for training and evaluating model performance.
Overfitting: Model learns training data too well, performs poorly on new data.
Underfitting: Model is too simple, fails to capture important data patterns.
Linear Regression: Models linear relationship for continuous output prediction.
Logistic Regression: Used for classification, predicts probability of class membership.
Decision Trees: Non-linear model splitting data into subsets based on features.
Random Forest: Ensemble method combining multiple decision trees for improved performance.
Support Vector Machines (SVM): Finds optimal hyperplane to separate data points for classification.
Neural Networks: Inspired by the brain, learns complex patterns, used in deep learning.
Healthcare: Disease diagnosis, drug discovery, personalized treatment.
Finance: Fraud detection, credit scoring, algorithmic trading.
Marketing: Customer segmentation, personalized recommendations, targeted advertising.
Autonomous Vehicles: Processing sensor data, decision-making, safe navigation.
Natural Language Processing (NLP): Language translation, sentiment analysis, text summarization.
Training and Testing: Evaluate performance using separate datasets with metrics (e.g., accuracy, MSE).
Cross-Validation: Technique to ensure model generalizes well to unseen data.
Hyperparameter Tuning: Optimizing model settings (hyperparameters) for optimal performance.

sections.heading: Challenges and Future of Machine Learning

bullets.text: Data Quality and Quantity: Requires large amounts of accurate data; collecting labeled data is challenging.
Interpretability: Complex models are often difficult to understand, especially in high-stakes applications.
Bias in Data: Models can inherit biases from training data, leading to unfair outcomes.
Overfitting and Underfitting: Common issues affecting model generalization.
Future: Advancements in deep learning, reinforcement learning, and explainable AI (XAI).
Ethical considerations and responsible AI practices will be essential.
